claims.explanation: Midodrine is an alpha-1 adrenergic agonist prodrug whose active metabolite causes vasoconstriction; its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is most plausibly explained by expression of the alpha-1 adrenergic receptor ADRA1A/ADRA1B, which signals through Gq/PLC to raise intracellular calcium and activate stress/anti-proliferative pathways in receptor-high lines. TP53 loss and RAS/MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NF1) appear enriched in sensitive lines, consistent with impaired stress responses and dependence on adrenergic/Gq signaling for survival. Lines with intact survival signaling through PI3K/AKT (PIK3CA, PTEN wild-type) or high ADRA1D (a low-affinity receptor) may be relatively protected.

features.basis: midodrine is an alpha-1 adrenergic agonist; receptor expression is required for Gq-mediated signaling
alpha-1 adrenergic receptor subtype mediating midodrine's vasoconstrictor and potential antiproliferative effects
TP53 mutations are highly enriched among selectively killed lines, suggesting loss of stress-induced survival/apoptosis control
KRAS-mutant lines (pancreas, colorectal) are overrepresented among sensitive lines, indicating MAPK-driven dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines appear among sensitive lines, consistent with MAPK pathway addiction
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is seen in several sensitive lines
PTEN loss with intact PI3K/AKT survival signaling is enriched in least-affected lines
PIK3CA mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting PI3K/AKT-mediated survival counteracts midodrine stress
ADRA1D is a low-affinity alpha-1 subtype; high expression may sequester drug without productive Gq signaling
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1437) are among least affected, suggesting RTK-driven survival
CDKN2A loss appears in several sensitive lines and may impair cell-cycle checkpoint response to adrenergic stress
NF2 mutations appear in sensitive pancreas, ovary, and thyroid lines, possibly via Hippo/YAP-mediated stress sensitivity
